sources.title: ASD Essential Eight maturity model (November 2023)
sources.locator: Appendices A (pp. 5–7), B (pp. 8–14), C (pp. 15–23), D comparison (pp. 24–33)

limitations: This is a partial, manually curated extraction; omitted statements remain an explicit coverage gap. Passing these rules is not an Essential Eight maturity determination.
Level 0 has no passable baseline in this pack. The pack only encodes expressly stated Level 1, 2 and 3 requirements.
Every fact is supplied by an operator. References and reviewer identifiers do not prove artifact authenticity, complete scope or actual enforcement.
Calendar months must be assessed from declared calendar dates; the engine must not approximate them as 30 days.
Scope, exceptions, compensating controls, business need and independent assessment remain matters for contextual human review.
This pack performs no network requests, authenticated configuration collection, attack execution, artifact replay or backup restoration.

requirements.label: Automated asset discovery interval
requirements.locator: Appendices A/B/C, Patch applications, asset discovery; printed pp. 5, 8, 15
requirements.interpretationNotes: Use the maximum observed discovery interval across the declared asset population and review period; one recent scan does not prove recurring coverage.

requirements.label: Current vulnerability database
requirements.locator: Appendices A/B/C, Patch applications, scanner database; printed pp. 5, 8, 15
requirements.interpretationNotes: Assess the complete declared asset population from sanitized operator evidence. A website observation alone does not establish this requirement.

requirements.label: Online service scan interval
requirements.locator: Appendices A/B/C, Patch applications, online-service vulnerability scanning; printed pp. 5, 8, 15
requirements.interpretationNotes: Assess the complete declared asset population from sanitized operator evidence. A website observation alone does not establish this requirement.

requirements.label: Common application scan interval
requirements.locator: Appendices A/B/C, Patch applications, commonly targeted application scanning; printed pp. 5, 8, 15
requirements.interpretationNotes: Include office suites, browsers and extensions, email clients, PDF software and security products. Scope completeness requires an inventory review.

requirements.label: Urgent online service patch delay
requirements.locator: Appendices A/B/C, Patch applications, critical or exploited online-service fixes; printed pp. 5, 8, 15
requirements.interpretationNotes: Measure from vendor release to verified deployment across all applicable fixes. This condition includes vendor-critical flaws OR a working exploit; missing severity information is not a safe exemption.

requirements.label: Other online service patch delay
requirements.locator: Appendices A/B/C, Patch applications, non-critical non-exploited online-service fixes; printed pp. 5, 8, 15
requirements.interpretationNotes: The declared applicability population excludes vendor-critical flaws and working exploits. Measure elapsed delay from release, using the worst applicable case.

requirements.label: Common application patch delay
requirements.locator: Appendices A/B, Patch applications, commonly targeted application fixes; printed pp. 5, 8
requirements.interpretationNotes: The population comprises office productivity suites, web browsers and extensions, email clients, PDF software and security products. The Level 3 urgency split is a separate rule; do not apply this lower-level threshold to critical or exploited Level 3 cases.

requirements.label: Urgent common application patch delay
requirements.locator: Appendix C, Patch applications, critical or exploited commonly targeted fixes; printed p. 15
requirements.interpretationNotes: Includes office suites, browsers and extensions, email clients, PDF software and security products. Condition is vendor-critical OR working exploit.

requirements.label: Other application scan interval
requirements.locator: Appendices B/C, Patch applications, other application vulnerability scanning; printed pp. 8, 15
requirements.interpretationNotes: Other applications excludes office productivity suites, web browsers and extensions, email clients, PDF software and security products. Measure the maximum scan interval across the assessment window and the reconciled inventory.

requirements.label: Other application calendar patch delay
requirements.locator: Appendices B/C, Patch applications, other application fixes; printed pp. 8, 15
requirements.interpretationNotes: Other applications excludes office productivity suites, web browsers and extensions, email clients, PDF software and security products. One month is a calendar unit. Operator evidence must declare the calendar calculation from release to deployment; do not approximate it as 30 days.

requirements.label: Urgent internet-facing OS patch delay
requirements.locator: Appendices A/B/C, Patch operating systems, critical or exploited internet-facing fixes; printed pp. 6, 9, 16
requirements.interpretationNotes: Population includes internet-facing servers and network devices. Vendor-critical OR working exploit triggers this deadline.

requirements.label: Other internet-facing OS patch delay
requirements.locator: Appendices A/B/C, Patch operating systems, non-critical non-exploited internet-facing fixes; printed pp. 6, 9, 16
requirements.interpretationNotes: Assess the complete declared asset population from sanitized operator evidence. A website observation alone does not establish this requirement.

requirements.label: Other OS calendar patch delay
requirements.locator: Appendices A/B, Patch operating systems, workstation and non-internet-facing fixes; printed pp. 6, 9
requirements.interpretationNotes: One month remains a calendar month. Workstations, internal servers and internal network devices are included; Level 3 urgent cases have a separate rule.

requirements.label: Urgent other OS patch delay
requirements.locator: Appendix C, Patch operating systems, critical or exploited workstation and non-internet-facing fixes; printed p. 16
requirements.interpretationNotes: Assess the complete declared asset population from sanitized operator evidence. A website observation alone does not establish this requirement.

requirements.label: Supported OS release position
requirements.locator: Appendix C, Patch operating systems, latest or previous release; printed p. 17
requirements.interpretationNotes: Zero denotes the latest release and one the previous release in the applicable vendor release sequence. This is not a version-number subtraction; an operator must identify the vendor sequence.

requirements.label: Sensitive workforce online MFA
requirements.locator: Appendices A/B/C, Multi-factor authentication, organisational and third-party sensitive online services; printed pp. 6, 9, 17
requirements.interpretationNotes: Cover every workforce user of the declared organisation-owned and third-party services handling sensitive organisational data. A visible login challenge is insufficient to establish complete enforcement.

requirements.label: System user MFA coverage
requirements.locator: Appendices B/C, Multi-factor authentication, privileged and unprivileged system users; printed pp. 9, 17
requirements.interpretationNotes: Assess the complete declared asset population from sanitized operator evidence. A website observation alone does not establish this requirement.

requirements.label: Repository user MFA coverage
requirements.locator: Appendix C, Multi-factor authentication, data-repository users; printed p. 17
requirements.interpretationNotes: Assess the complete declared asset population from sanitized operator evidence. A website observation alone does not establish this requirement.

requirements.label: Workforce online phishing resistance
requirements.locator: Appendices B/C, Multi-factor authentication, online-service phishing resistance; printed pp. 10, 17
requirements.interpretationNotes: This clause qualifies MFA actually used for workforce online services. A third-party service processing only non-sensitive data without available MFA does not itself trigger a phishing-resistance violation. MFA absence for the separately applicable sensitive-service populations is assessed by the base MFA coverage rules. Evaluate all used MFA mechanisms and fallback paths from scoped evidence; false applicability remains subject to review.

requirements.label: Customer resistant MFA option
requirements.locator: Appendix B, Multi-factor authentication, customer-service phishing-resistant option; printed p. 10
requirements.interpretationNotes: Level 2 requires an available resistant option. Level 3 has a separate requirement for the customer authentication actually used.

requirements.label: Customer enforced phishing resistance
requirements.locator: Appendix C, Multi-factor authentication, customer-service phishing resistance; printed p. 17
requirements.interpretationNotes: Assess the complete declared asset population from sanitized operator evidence. A website observation alone does not establish this requirement.

requirements.label: Privileged access revalidation interval
requirements.locator: Appendices B/C, Restrict administrative privileges, 12-month revalidation; printed pp. 10, 18
requirements.interpretationNotes: Use calendar months for active system, application and data-repository grants. Grants older than the interval need renewed validation or removal; a policy statement alone does not prove enforcement.

requirements.label: Inactive privilege disable delay
requirements.locator: Appendices B/C, Restrict administrative privileges, 45-day inactivity; printed pp. 10, 18
requirements.interpretationNotes: This clause names systems and applications. Include actual account inactivity/disable transitions across the declared population; do not silently extend the same deadline to unrelated grant types.

requirements.locator: Appendix C, Regular backups, backup-administrator retention restrictions; printed p. 23
requirements.interpretationNotes: Evaluate write/delete restrictions for backup administrators during the declared retention window; general user permissions do not establish this stronger Level 3 control.
